title: Shortest distances from one source
description:
Every edge of a weighted, undirected graph has a non-negative length. The distance from one vertex to another is the smallest total length of any path between them.

Implement a struct type called Edge with two integer fields: To, the vertex at the other end of the edge, and Weight, its length. Then implement a function called ShortestDistances that receives the number of vertices, an adjacency list, and a source vertex, and returns a list holding, for each vertex, its distance from the source. Vertices are numbered from zero. The adjacency list gives, for each vertex, the edges leaving it, and every edge appears in both directions.

With the edges 0-1 (length 4), 0-2 (8), 1-2 (3), 1-4 (6), 2-3 (2), 3-4 (10) and source 0:
ShortestDistances(5, adjacency, 0) -> [0, 4, 7, 9, 10]. Vertex 2 is reached through 1 for 4 + 3 = 7, which is shorter than the direct edge of 8, and vertex 3 is reached through 1 and then 2 for 7 + 2 = 9.

A vertex that cannot be reached from the source at all gets -1: with only the edge 0-1 (length 3) among three vertices, ShortestDistances(3, adjacency, 0) -> [0, 3, -1].

The hidden tests also check parallel edges between the same two vertices, where only the shortest one counts; edges of length zero; and a path of many short edges that beats a single long one.

This card asks for the optimal solution, and the tests enforce it: one of them is a graph of two hundred thousand vertices with a two second budget. Scanning every vertex on each step to find the closest one that is still unsettled gives the right answer but is far too slow to pass. The next vertex to settle has to come out of a priority queue, and the total work has to stay close to the number of edges times the logarithm of the number of vertices.
objective: Recall and implement Dijkstra's shortest-path algorithm with a min-heap, including skipping stale queue entries and reporting unreachable vertices.

metadata.source: Dijkstra's Algorithm to find Shortest Paths from a Source to all, GeeksforGeeks (https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/dsa/dijkstras-shortest-path-algorithm-greedy-algo-7/)
